q: Which corporate action does NOT change a company's market capitalisation?
e: Bonus issue (and stock split) only changes the share count and per-share price proportionally — total market cap is unchanged. Cash dividends reduce cap; buybacks reduce cap; M&A changes the entity entirely.

q: After a 1:1 bonus issue, the share count and per-share price will:
e: 1:1 bonus = one new free share for each existing share → shares double. Market cap unchanged → per-share price halves.

o: Tax-free for both company and shareholder
Paid by the shareholder at slab rate
Paid by the company at 23.296%; tax-free in shareholder's hands
e: Post-FY20: company pays 23.296% buyback tax on the distributed amount; receipt is tax-free for the shareholder. This was changed to align with the abolition of DDT.

q: An open offer under SAST is triggered when an acquirer's stake crosses:
e: Crossing 25% stake triggers a mandatory open offer for an additional 26% under SEBI (SAST) Regulations. Designed to give other shareholders an exit when control changes hands.

q: DDT (Dividend Distribution Tax) was abolished effective:
e: DDT was abolished from April 1, 2020 (FY 21 onwards). Dividends now taxable in shareholder's hands at slab rate; TDS at 10% if dividend > ₹5,000 per fiscal year.

q: For an extraordinary dividend, derivative strikes are adjusted only if the dividend exceeds:
e: Derivative strikes are adjusted for extraordinary cash dividends only if the dividend > 5% of stock price; smaller dividends are absorbed in normal trading.
